message.content: In lions, one of the most striking examples of a dominant genetic trait is the development of the mane in adult male lions. The presence of a mane is controlled by a dominant allele (often referred to as **M**), while the absence of a mane (or a very small mane) is associated with the recessive allele (**m**). Thus, if a male lion inherits at least one copy of the dominant **M** allele from either parent, he will develop a full mane. This trait is not only visually prominent but also plays a role in social signaling and mate selection within lion prides.
